cases.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?

answer.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?
answer.answer:
The client's daily report shows more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12 because it counts all attempts before any QC rollbacks are applied, while our dashboard removes rolled-back attempts from the door count. The difference consists of repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back due to QC flags like flash knocking.

- Client report counts attempts before rollbacks [doc:client-reporting#daily-report]
- Our dashboard removes rolled-back attempts from doors and contacts [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- The gap equals repeat attempts plus rolled-back attempts [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]

args.query: why client daily report differs from our doors gap repeat attempts rolled-back attempts

sources.text: The client daily report counts attempts, pulled at the end of each day before any QC rollback. Our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed. The gap on any day is the repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back. A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts. A larger gap almost always means a rollback.

The client receives a daily report per office pulled from the canvassing app at the end of each day. It lists attempts (labeled "doors" in the client's sheet) and contacts as submitted, before any QC rollback. We do not edit a daily report after it is sent.

When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is defined as recording doors faster than a person can physically walk to them and knock. Specifically, a shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. When confirmed, these knocks are rolled back and no longer count as doors or contacts.

- Flash knocking: 10+ consecutive knocks recorded less than 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Consequence: Confirmed flash knocking knocks are rolled back (removed from doors/contacts) [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- QC rate calculation uses flags per 100 GOTV shifts, not raw counts [doc:qc-rules#qc-rate]

sources.text: Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.
The QC rate is flags per 100 GOTV shifts for an office in a week. Week over week trends use this rate, not raw flag counts, because the number of shifts grows during the program.

answer.answer:
Payroll runs on Tuesday at noon for the week that ended Sunday. Overtime requires field director approval when a shift takes a person over 40 hours in a Monday-to-Sunday week, and all shifts must be approved by Monday at 5 PM to be included in that payroll.

answer.question: How should a canvasser record a locked apartment building?
answer.answer:
A canvasser should record a locked apartment building once as "inaccessible" on its first unit and then move on; they should not mark each individual unit. Marking a whole building from the lobby would be considered householding.

sources.text: Pace compares doors to date with the goal to date. The projection for Election Day assumes nothing changes: doors to date plus the average daily doors of the last 7 days times the knocking days left. An office "will miss goal" when its projection is below its total goal; the shortfall is the goal minus the projection.

The client daily report counts attempts, pulled at the end of each day before any QC rollback. Our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed. The gap on any day is the repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back. A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts. A larger gap almost always means a rollback.
